content.thinking: Actually the real issue might be how the printer handles replacement for multiline matches—it may re-run the match against a larger buffer than a single line, using different matching semantics. I should check standard.rs's replace logic for the multi-line sink path.
I want to check how Replacer::replace_all is implemented in util.rs.

I'm realizing the real issue is that the match re-executes starting at range.start against the subject with extra look-ahead content appended past range.end—so capture groups like an optional trailing usage comment can end up matching further than intended since that appended context is included in the search.

Since the extended context reveals more trailing lines, the optional trailing group could backtrack differently and consume further than intended, potentially explaining why the match grows without the -r flag—likely because the unbounded lookahead buffer lets the engine match more of the function signature across lines than the original single-line context would allow.

I think I've found the real bug: the extended subject given to captures_iter_at for look-ahead purposes includes bytes past the match's end, so it can find and process additional matches beyond the intended single-match range, appending their unmatched text into dst and producing the extra output — even though replace_all is meant to handle just one specific match range per SinkMatch call.

If a second match occurs in that look-ahead area, its replacement plus the unmatched gap bytes get appended verbatim - explaining the stray unreplaced content after the intended replacement. The real fix is to compute the replacement for only the single match in `range` using a single find_at/captures_at call, rather than the iterator-based multi-replace that keeps matching beyond it. I should check the original replace_all logic and any historical truncation behavior, and look further past line 110 for how MAX_LOOK_AHEAD is used.

This confirms the bug: replace_all iterates through all matches from range.start to the end of subject, so when multi-line mode extends subject past range.end via the look-ahead, extra unwanted matches in that region get swept up and included in the output too.

I should check how `replace` is actually invoked in standard.rs — the caller passes bytes as the full buffer and range as the exact bounds of one detected match, then extends the search into a look-ahead region for boundary matching. The simplest fix is to stop the append callback after the first match found within that range, then copy over any trailing content after it, since the call is meant to represent exactly one match rather than multiple.

Now I see the real bug: at the end, the code appends everything from the last match position to the end of the haystack (which includes the look-ahead extension), instead of stopping at range.end. So even when only one true match is found, the trailing append copies the entire look-ahead region as extra unwanted content — this matches exactly the reported bug behavior.

The fix should bound that trailing copy to range.end rather than the extended subject's actual end, so the look-ahead buffer used for multi-line matching doesn't leak into the output.

Instead of relying on replace_with_captures_at's automatic trailing append, I should write a custom loop using captures_iter_at directly, so I control exactly what gets appended after matching finishes -- only copying haystack up through range.end, never past it.

Fix confirmed and matches expected behavior. Also ran full `grep-printer` test suite (94/94 passed). Not committing per instructions.

## Summary

**Root cause**: `Replacer::replace_all` in `crates/printer/src/util.rs` handled multi-line replacements by extending the searched `subject` slice past `range.end` with extra look-ahead bytes (`MAX_LOOK_AHEAD`) so regex look-around could see beyond the current match. It then delegated to `Matcher::replace_with_captures_at`, which iterates *all* matches in that extended subject and, at the end, blindly copies everything from the last match to the end of `subject` into the output. Since `subject` included the look-ahead bytes, this trailing copy leaked unrelated content (and any additional matches found in the look-ahead region) into the replacement output.

**Fix**: Replaced the call to `replace_with_captures_at` with a manual loop using `captures_iter_at` that:
- keeps replacing all matches whose start is within `range` (preserving existing multi-match-per-line behavior),
- stops as soon as a match starts at or beyond `range.end` (i.e., it only exists because of the look-ahead bytes), and
- bounds the final trailing unmatched-byte copy to `range.end` instead of the full (look-ahead-extended) `subject`.

This is scoped to `crates/printer/src/util.rs` only.
